title: Ruby in the Dust. Poetry and History in Padmāvat by the South Asian Sufi Poet Muhammad Jāyasī
author: তথ্য নেই
description: This book presents an innovative reading of the Indian mystical romance Padmāvat (1540). It describes the semantic polyphony of Jāyasī’s seminal work from the perspective of the poet’s role in the literary field, as mediator between the interests of his spiritual and worldly patrons. The contextual outlook of De Bruijn’s interpretation corrects the identification with modern, nationalist notions of Hindu and Muslim identity that have dominated readings of Padmāvat until now. De Bruijn’s reading reveals the confluence of poetry and history that inspired the many retellings of the tale of Padmāvatī and Ratansen in Persian and other Indian languages.

description: The urban sufism movement namely Hubbun Nabi becomes an interesting phenomenon since it emerges in the midst of Islamic-militant religious movement which is symptomatic in Sukoharjo. This research portrayed the style of moderate religiosity which is developed by Majlis Dzikir and Sholawat Hubbun Nabi. It was a descriptive-qualitative research. description: “Niyaz wa Fatiha ka Shar‘i Suboot” is an Islamic book that presents the scholarly evidence and reasoning for the validity and permissibility of Niyaz and Fatiha in light of the Qur’an, Hadith, and opinions of classical scholars (Ulama). The book explains that offering charity and food (Niyaz) and reciting Fatiha for the souls of the Prophet ﷺ, Ahl al-Bayt, and pious saints is a means of Eesal-e-Sawab (conveying rewards) — a practice deeply rooted in Islamic tradition. It refutes misconceptions and objections raised by certain groups, proving through authentic references that such acts are not innovations (Bid‘ah) but rather expressions of love, gratitude, and remembrance of Allah and His beloved servants.
